cards.title: Analog Clock
cards.alt: Pendulum clock on a stand, with the movement visible behind the dial
cards.body: Only one part of a clock keeps time, and it is not the gears. The pendulum is the ruler and the wheels are a counter — 43 200 beats to one turn of the hour hand. Take the dial and the case away to watch the train do the counting, then move the rating nut one millimetre and watch 43 seconds a day appear out of nowhere.

cards.title: Scissor Lift
cards.alt: Motorised hydraulic scissor lift on castors, raising a load
cards.body: Two rams, a linkage, and a mechanical advantage that will not sit still. Flat on the floor the rams push twenty times the weight they are lifting; near the top, twice. Watch the pressure gauge collapse as it rises — then watch the speed do the opposite, and work out why those are the same fact.

cards.title: 6-Axis Robot Arm
cards.alt: Industrial robot arm lifting a carton onto a moving conveyor
cards.body: An industrial arm picking parts off a table and setting them on a moving belt. Six revolute joints, solved with the cosine rule; watch the shoulder torque climb as the load goes out to arm's length, and find the acceleration that pulls the part off the tool.

cards.title: 3D Printer
cards.alt: 3D printer building an object layer by layer
cards.body: How a machine builds a solid object by adding one layer at a time. Set the layer height, speed and temperatures, watch the X, Y and Z axes move as the nozzle traces each slice, and print the pot in four colours off the four-spool AMS. Slow motion drops it to real time, to watch a single line actually go down.

cards.title: Bench Drill
cards.alt: Bench drill with the belt drive visible through a clear guard
cards.body: One motor at one speed, and a belt on five pairs of pulleys to turn it into five. Move the belt and watch speed and turning effort trade off exactly. Then try to stall it: on the low steps the belt slips first, on the high ones the motor gives out — and changing gear turns out to be no help at all against the second one.

cards.title: Centre Lathe
cards.alt: Centre lathe turning a bar down in the chuck
cards.body: The machine where the cutting speed will not stay put. Every pass makes the bar thinner, so the speed the edge sees falls away while you work — and facing to the centre takes it to zero. The companion piece to the bench drill, and it inverts the drill’s lesson: here, spinning faster really does finish the job sooner.

cards.title: Walschaerts Valve Gear
cards.body: How a locomotive times steam into a double-acting cylinder. Adjust cut-off and reversing, watch the piston valve distribute live and exhaust steam, and hear the exhaust beat.

cards.title: Rotary to Linear Motion
cards.body: A crank-rocker driving a toothed rack. Vary the crank length to cross the Grashof limit and see continuous rotation give way to a linkage that can no longer turn.

cards.title: Scotch Yoke Mechanism
cards.body: A pin running in a slotted yoke, turning rotation into exact simple harmonic motion. Watch displacement trace a true cosine while the crank turns steadily.

cards.title: Aircraft Landing Gear
cards.body: Land an airliner and watch the strut absorb it. Momentum, impulse and Hooke’s law, with live force and compression graphs showing why a longer impact means a gentler one.

cards.title: Car Gearbox
cards.body: Start the engine, pick a gear and drive. Watch a small gear turn a big one into strong slow torque — and see on the dials why a hill wants first gear and a motorway wants fifth.

cards.title: Differential Gear — 2D
cards.body: Round a bend the outer wheel has further to go. Watch the spider gears spin to let it, check that the two wheel speeds always average to the carrier — then put one wheel on ice and see why the car goes nowhere.

cards.title: Differential Gear — 3D
cards.body: The same physics on a real three-dimensional differential you can turn round and look into. Hold one wheel still and watch the other run at exactly twice the carrier speed.
